items.stem: A program appends to a collection millions of times and only ever reads from the end. Which structure gives the best amortised performance with the least memory overhead?

options.rationale: Correct: a dynamic array gives amortised O(1) append and has no per-element pointer overhead.
A doubly linked list appends in O(1) but carries two pointers per node, wasting memory for this pattern.
A BST adds O(log n) per insert and ordering you do not need here.
A hash set does not preserve insertion order and adds hashing overhead for no benefit.

items.explanation: Correct: a dynamic array gives amortised O(1) append and has no per-element pointer overhead.

items.stem: A hash table with chaining is showing lookups far slower than O(1). Which single cause most directly explains this?

options.text: A high load factor with a poor hash spreading keys into few buckets
options.rationale: Correct: a high load factor plus poor distribution lengthens chains, pushing lookups toward O(n).

options.text: The table stores strings instead of integers
options.rationale: Key type alone does not break O(1) if the hash distributes well.

options.text: The table was created with a capacity hint
options.rationale: A capacity hint reduces resizes and generally helps, not hurts.
The scenario states chaining, not open addressing.

items.explanation: Correct: a high load factor plus poor distribution lengthens chains, pushing lookups toward O(n).

items.stem: Which TWO statements about binary search are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It requires the input to be sorted on the search key
options.rationale: Correct: binary search relies on ordering to discard half the range each step.

options.text: It runs in O(log n) comparisons on a sorted array
options.rationale: Correct: each step halves the search range, giving logarithmic comparisons.

options.text: It works in O(log n) on an unsorted array
options.rationale: Without ordering the halving assumption fails; you would need a linear scan.
Binary search uses comparisons and ordering, not hashing.

items.explanation: Correct: binary search relies on ordering to discard half the range each step.
